name: Mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order ten
description: construct() -> a nonempty list of 10-by-10 arrays with Python integer symbols 0..9. Every row and column must contain each symbol exactly once. For every two arrays, their 100 ordered symbol pairs must be distinct. Maximize the number of pairwise orthogonal arrays. Only order ten is evaluated. The cyclic single-square baseline does not implement Wilson’s recursive constructions. No current best-known N(10), global optimality or novel family is asserted.

sources.locator: Richard M. Wilson, Concerning the number of mutually orthogonal latin squares (1974). Publisher abstract defines N(n), the maximum size of a mutually orthogonal family, and proves general lower bounds through combinatorial constructions.

state_of_the_art.statement: Two orthogonal Latin squares of order 10 exist (Parker 1959), and no set of three has been found. Since there is no projective plane of order 10 (Lam, Thiel and Swiercz 1989), at most 8 are possible. The growth of N(n) is Erdős Problem #724.
